page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a virtual machine instance belonging to the High Performance server family, configured with 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, structured with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. CPU resources are allocated on a shared basis. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of a 32 KB L1d cache, a 4 MB L2 cache, and a 16 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES cryptography, and FMA. Local storage is bundled with a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities but overall constrained multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test achieved a score of 1455.08, placing it in the average tier, whereas the multi-core CPU test yielded a weak score of 2890.77. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; read-only small block cached memory bandwidth reached 206.26 GB/sec, but large-block uncached read and write bandwidths dropped to 16.98 GB/sec and 14.27 GB/sec respectively, both falling into the poor category. Passmark testing aligns with these results, showing a weak CPU score of 3215.34 and a poor encryption score of 1051.12. Database operations and static web serving throughput are also limited, with the latter recorded at 2.61 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point with bundled NVMe storage, making it suitable for lightweight workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The shared CPU allocation and weak multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs for compute-intensive tasks. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight application hosting, development environments, and simple background tasks. It is less suitable for database hosting, large-scale data processing, or real-time LLM inference, as demonstrated by the poor prompt processing speed of 138.3 tokens/second on a small 135M model.
description: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a shared-CPU virtual machine from the High Performance family, featuring 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, it includes 1 physical core with hyper-threading, a 16 MB L3 cache, and a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1455.08, but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth results. Large-block memory write speeds are limited to 14.27 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput reaches 2.61 GB/sec. Given its shared CPU allocation and low resource density, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for low-intensity applications. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, development environments, and basic background processing, while being poorly suited for database operations or memory-intensive workloads.
